findings.title: Officials suspect Iran in series of cyberattacks on military base freezers
findings.summary_md: Nextgov/FCW reports that U.S. officials suspect Iran-linked hackers in freezer malfunctions at military bases across the country, with incidents beginning around late August and roughly six commissaries affected. The Pentagon was treating the events as possible cyberattacks. This is the earliest dated disclosure of the suspected actor behind the refrigeration incidents.

findings.title: Officials suspect Iran of cyberattacks on military base freezers
findings.summary_md: Defense One carries the Nextgov/FCW reporting dated November 2, 2026, that officials suspect Iran-linked hackers in military freezer failures at commissaries. This is the first broad news pickup of the suspected Iranian involvement, three days before the federal warning.

findings.title: Supermarket freezers across Europe hit by second suspected cyber-attack
findings.summary_md: The Guardian reports a second wave of suspected cyberattacks on supermarket refrigerators across Europe on November 2, affecting stores in Belgium, Ireland, Luxembourg and Sweden, with an ICA store in Sjoebo, Sweden, having its fridges and freezers set to 50 degrees Celsius. Days earlier, hacks forced grocery stores across eight European countries to discard spoiled food.

findings.title: Blood banks targeted in latest European fridge cyberattacks
findings.summary_md: CNBC reports that several French regional blood banks were hit by a cyberattack on November 2 in which attackers attempted to raise storage temperatures to extremely high levels. The French health ministry said no blood products were compromised and the situation was under control. The incident followed the European supermarket refrigeration attacks.
